verdicts.quote: Default schedule is offsets **-3, 0, +7, +14** calendar days from the invoice due date, sent at **09:00** account-local time.
An invoice is *open* (eligible) when it is issued (not draft), not void or cancelled, has outstanding balance > 0 and has a due date.
verdicts.missing: Full payment and voiding stop reminders, and partial payment leaves them active. The spec gives no rule for a credit that leaves a balance, a dispute, or a payment plan.

verdicts.quote: A partial payment keeps the invoice open and the next reminder states the reduced outstanding amount.
Compliance and legal content rules for payment-reminder email (identification, opt-out, jurisdiction).
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say whether an existing do-not-contact flag, pause, or unsubscribe suppresses reminders, or whether billing notices are exempt from a marketing opt-out.

verdicts.quote:
The only duplicate window is the crash-after-accept case below. It is bounded by A-8 (at most 3 emails
  for one occurrence).
verdicts.missing: Concurrent runs are guarded, but retry after a crash between provider acceptance and recording Sent can send the same reminder again. Duplicate prevention across that retry is missing.

verdicts.quote:
An occurrence is sent only if, **at the moment it is claimed for sending**, the authoritative invoice
  state says the invoice is open (A-3).

Transient failure (timeout, provider unavailable, rate limit, unreadable invoice state): the occurrence stays Pending,
    the attempt counts, and it is retried at the next processing run. The third failed attempt ends as
    Failed(`attempts-exhausted`) (T-11).
verdicts.missing: Exhausted attempts appear in a failed-reminders list. The spec does not say who is alerted or how the failure is escalated to them.

verdicts.quote: invoice volume, provider rate limits and run cadence are unknown.
verdicts.missing: The spec retries rate-limit responses but leaves the applicable quota and the pacing of a large batch within that quota open.

verdicts.quote: Enabling, editing or re-planning does **not** backfill occurrences whose date has already passed; they are skipped.
Offsets are plain calendar days: no business-day or holiday calendar.
verdicts.missing: The schedule uses account-local time and permits any send time. It provides no customer-local business-hours rule for a recipient in another time zone.

verdicts.quote:
A currency's own decimal places are preserved as the product
  already formats them.

No billing contact: Skipped(`no-recipient`), terminal, and later occurrences are evaluated afresh (T-9).
  - Permanent rejection of the address by the provider: Failed(`rejected`), no retry (T-10).
Where the billing contact lives and whether there can be several. | R-3, R-6 | One address per invoice.
verdicts.missing: Only one address is used. The rule for choosing it when several billing contacts exist is unspecified.

verdicts.quote:
Per invoice, an authorized user can see every occurrence: offset, scheduled local date and time, status (Pending,
    Sent, Skipped, Cancelled, Failed), reason, sent time and recipient used.
verdicts.missing: The history identifies the step, time and recipient, but provides no way to see the message content or the balance actually quoted at send time.

verdicts.quote: If the product has a payment link or payment instructions today, they are included as-is (G-1).
verdicts.missing: The message includes the invoice number, current amount and due date. The validity period of an existing payment link and the handling of an expired link are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: a user who can manage invoices may read and change reminder settings.
verdicts.missing: Invoice managers can disable reminders account-wide, and manual send is excluded. The spec does not expressly settle who, if anyone, may cancel a single pending reminder by hand.

verdicts.quote: An authorized user of an account can enable or disable reminders for the account and set the schedule.
verdicts.missing: Per-customer opt-out and manual send are explicitly excluded. There is no preview or dry-run policy.

verdicts.quote:
Per invoice, an authorized user can see every occurrence: offset, scheduled local date and time, status (Pending,
    Sent, Skipped, Cancelled, Failed), reason, sent time and recipient used.
So a customer never gets more than one reminder per invoice per run.
reminders only read invoice and payment data and never write it (R-2).
